summary: A structural read of data/master.json (generated 2026-10-21, 369 rows). It checks what can be checked without re-fetching every fixture: dates, source links, duplicate identity, prediction length and vocabulary, confidence labels and sport scoping. Each finding names the rows it touches and links the body that could settle it.

findings.title: Rows dated before the review date
findings.detail: 210 of 369 rows carry a date before 2026-10-24. A stale row is not automatically wrong, but it cannot be a live quote: the price beside it was built for a fixture that has already started or been played.
examples: Anadolu Efes Istanbul @ Crvena Zvezda Belgrade (M0003)
Rafael Jódar (ESP) Runner-up @ Alejandro Davidovich Fokina (ESP) Champion (M0004)

findings.title: Rows with no source URL
findings.detail: 39 rows publish a price and a pick with an empty source_url field. The reader has no click-through, which breaks the rule that every row links the body it came from.
examples: Anadolu Efes Istanbul @ Crvena Zvezda Belgrade (M0003)
Rafael Jódar (ESP) Runner-up @ Alejandro Davidovich Fokina (ESP) Champion (M0004)

findings.title: The same fixture appears more than once
findings.detail: 0 rows share a sport, both team names and a date with another row. A duplicated fixture produces two prices for one market, and a reader cannot tell which is current.

findings.title: Written predictions below the 30-word floor
findings.detail: 0 rows carry a prediction shorter than the brief's 30-word minimum, which makes them bare winner calls rather than analysis.

findings.title: Predictions using the excluded vocabulary
findings.detail: 35 predictions contain a word the brief excludes from output text (the model/verification vocabulary). These read as machine provenance, not as a tip.

findings.title: Rows with no confidence label
findings.detail: 50 rows publish a pick without a High/Medium/Low label, so the reader cannot tell a strong opinion from a coin-flip.

findings.title: Rows outside the fifteen-sport brief
findings.detail: 11 rows belong to a sport the brief excludes (Aussie Rules, Badminton, Esports, Greyhound Racing, Table Tennis).
examples: Field Europe top-32 @ Winners to be verified via ETTU (M0008)
TBD per BWF results page @ Winners: FRA Alex Lanier, KOR An Se-young, INA Alfian/Fikri, MAS Tan/Muralitharan, CHN Jiang/Wei (M0009)

findings.title: Gaelic Football rows sit outside the scope list
findings.detail: 5 rows use the label Gaelic Football while the file's scope list uses Gaelic Sports, so a scope filter silently drops them.

findings.title: One sport under two labels
findings.detail: 8 rows are split across Greyhound Racing, Greyhounds. Two labels for one sport break per-sport counts and make the coverage table disagree with itself.

findings.title: Sports represented by fewer than five rows
findings.detail: 13 rows belong to a sport with under five fixtures — too few to support the brief's five predictions per sport.
examples: Field Europe top-32 @ Winners to be verified via ETTU (M0008)
